mathematical_scope: Lines 8–32 construct an m=N/2 quadratic-chirp Hankel matrix over a field with a primitive 2N-th root. The diagonal–Vandermonde factorization is algebraically correct: (a+b)^2=a^2+b^2+2ab and omega=xi^2. Distinct evaluation points give rank m. Lines 35–61 check the separated half-cut of a sum of q diagonal-gauged inverse path-tridiagonals with one common path order. A common-order cut has rank at most q, while the Fourier consecutive-row/consecutive-column cut is Vandermonde of rank m. These are architecture-specific additive barriers.
input_and_guard_coverage: Chirp entry asserts even N>=2; common-order entry asserts even N>2 and q<N/2. Neither enforces integer arguments or q>=1. q=0 or negative passes the latter guard, then max(component_ranks) fails on an empty list. Assertions are not durable input checks under Python -O. Root/field validity is inherited from green_sum_cert.
cost_and_scaling: Dense Hankel/Fourier construction uses quadratic storage/work (plus modular exponent costs), and rank elimination is cubic in m. The all-entry Bluestein verification adds N² modular exponentiations. q Green submatrices require q·m tridiagonal solves. This is a dense certificate generator, not a fast Fourier implementation.
test_evidence: Test_phase17 tests 7–9 cover N=8..128 for chirps and N=16,32,64 for common-order q=2. No q=0, negative q, odd size, root-search failure, or optimized-assertion mode tests. Tests read only; never run here.
